clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. She exhibited a generally cheerful and cooperative demeanor; however, she demonstrated fluctuations in attention span and a tendency towards distractibility, affecting her sustained engagement in tasks. Muscle tone and range of motion were within normal limits, consistent with her age expectations. During activities requiring focused engagement, Sabrina showed a preference for self-directed tasks, yet required maximal verbal and visual cues during structured activities to maintain participation. Fine motor tasks revealed challenges with visual-motor integration, necessitating hand-over-hand assistance to successfully complete certain manipulative activities. Her need for frequent redirection and cues led to the implementation of testing modifications, impacting the validity of standardized outcomes. Certain behaviors observed, such as task avoidance when demands increased, further highlighted the necessity for adapted strategies to support her performance effectively.
